title: Good Quantum Locally Testable Codes from Product Expansion
authors: Mitali Bafna, Anqi Li, Quynh T. Nguyen
abstract: We construct quantum locally testable codes (LTCs) with constant rate, distance, soundness and locality under a variant of a product expansion conjecture of Bafna and Vyas about Reed-Solomon codes. In particular, we use the high-dimensional expansion framework of Dinur, Lin and Vidick for constructing quantum LTCs, instantiated with the non-Abelian cubical complexes of Rungtanapirom, Stix and Vdovina. Our code is obtained by equipping the complex with carefully chosen Reed-Solomon local codes whose symmetries are compatible with those of the complex.
summary: This paper develops a method to construct high-quality Quantum Locally Testable Codes (qLTCs) by combining concepts from algebraic topology and coding theory. It overcomes previous limitations by employing non-Abelian cubical complexes within a high-dimensional expansion framework. The result provides a theoretical blueprint for building quantum codes with excellent, constant performance guarantees.
main_problem: The primary goal is to construct quantum locally testable codes (qLTCs) that possess desirable constant parameters (rate, distance, soundness, locality).
main_result: The authors construct an explicit family of good qLTCs by leveraging a variant of the product expansion conjecture and utilizing non-Abelian cubical complexes.
method: The construction method involves equipping high-dimensional non-Abelian cubical complexes with carefully chosen Reed-Solomon local codes whose symmetries are compatible with the complex structure.
model_or_system: The model is Quantum Locally Testable Codes (qLTCs), which are defined using CSS codes derived from underlying graph/complex structures, generalizing from 2D to higher dimensions.
key_observables: Constant rate, quantum distance, soundness, and locality of the constructed code.
important_parameters: The construction requires the local codes to satisfy a $ho$-product-expanding property, and the rate must be non-zero.
main_assumptions: The construction critically relies on assuming a variant of the product expansion conjecture of Bafna and Vyas.
paper_structure: The paper builds by first reviewing classical LTCs on Cayley Complexes, then generalizing to the high-dimensional expansion framework, and finally improving the construction by incorporating non-Abelian cubical complexes and RS codes.
why_interesting: This work provides advanced theoretical tools for constructing robust quantum error-correcting codes, which are foundational for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
